definitions.explanation: Done regularly as a habit or established custom, rather than as a one-time action.

examples.japanese: {習慣的|しゅうかんてき}に{運動|うんどう}する。
{習慣的|しゅうかんてき}な{飲酒|いんしゅ}は{健康|けんこう}に{悪|わる}い。
examples.english: Habitual drinking is bad for your health.

examples.japanese: {朝|あさ}の{散歩|さんぽ}が{習慣的|しゅうかんてき}な{行動|こうどう}になっている。
examples.english: Morning walks have become a habitual part of my routine.

notes:
Derived from {習慣|しゅうかん} (habit; custom) plus {的|てき}. Describes actions or behaviors that are performed regularly over time. Can be used both positively (good habits) and negatively (bad habits). Often appears in medical and health-related contexts.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {習慣的|しゅうかんてき}な{行動|こうどう}: habitual behavior
- {習慣的|しゅうかんてき}な{飲酒|いんしゅ}: habitual drinking
- {習慣的|しゅうかんてき}な{喫煙|きつえん}: habitual smoking
- {習慣的|しゅうかんてき}に{行|おこな}う: to do habitually

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {日常的|にちじょうてき}: everyday; daily — describes what happens in ordinary daily life, without implying deliberate repetition
- {恒常的|こうじょうてき}: constant; permanent — emphasizes unchanging continuity rather than repeated habit
- {慢性的|まんせいてき}: chronic — used mainly in medical or problem contexts to describe persistent conditions
